cues.zh: 可口可乐这样的公司，就特别喜欢这种

cues.zh: 能量平衡范式，也就是这种

cues.zh: 你不能创造它，也不能摧毁它。因此，要么是卡路里摄入，要么是卡路里消耗。现在这确实有两个主要问题。

cues.en: And

cues.en: So there's really two fundamental errors in this whole idea of calories in, calories out. Right?
cues.zh: 所以这个“卡路里摄入，卡路里消耗”的整个想法中确实有两个根本错误。对吧？

cues.zh: 他们认为热量是一个单一区室，而肥胖其实是一个双区室问题。

cues.en: That is, there are different ways for your body to use that energy that you put in. You can burn it or you can store it as fat. Right? So there's two different pathways.
cues.zh: 也就是说，你摄入的能量，身体有不同的使用方式。你可以把它燃烧掉，也可以把它储存为脂肪。对吧？所以有两条不同的路径。

cues.zh: 重要的是你走哪条路径，

cues.en: not the total energy of the system.
cues.zh: 而不是系统的总能量。

cues.zh: 但我们先谈谈近因与根本原因。什么是近因？近因就是最接近的那个原因。

cues.zh: 所以如果你担心肥胖，肥胖的近因就是热量太多。对吧？那就是直接发生在它之前的原因。

cues.zh: 但最终导致它发生的，是根本原因。明白吗？

cues.en: So the thing is if you treat the proximate cause, it's kind of futile. It doesn't really work. If you treat the ultimate cause, because that's what's really underlying this disease,
cues.zh: 所以问题是，如果你去治近因，那有点徒劳。它并不真的有效。如果你去治根本原因，因为那才是这个疾病真正的根源，

cues.zh: 对吧？你可以说，酗酒

cues.zh: 对吧？那么

cues.zh: 这是一条基本定律。

cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.zh: 对吧？你不能创造

cues.zh: 那只是近因。

cues.zh: 他们所做的，当然是采用了大约50%碳水化合物的

cues.en: diet, right? So they went up from 44.5
cues.zh: 饮食，对吧？所以从44.5

cues.en: And if you look at fat, right, fat went from 38.8
cues.zh: 再看脂肪，对吧，脂肪从38.8

cues.en: Great. Terrific.
cues.zh: 很好。太棒了。

cues.en: Low calorie, low fat diet. Right? Love it.
cues.zh: 低热量、低脂饮食。对吧？爱了。

cues.en: What happened?
cues.zh: 结果呢？

cues.en: Well, it didn't work. Right? These people who should have lost 36 pounds every single year
cues.zh: 嗯，没起作用。对吧？这些人本应每年减掉36磅

cues.en: didn't even lose a single pound,
cues.zh: 结果连一磅都没减掉，

cues.en: like, in ten years almost.
cues.zh: 差不多十年里都是如此。

cues.en: Right? Not a single pound. They should have lost, like, you know, 210 pounds of fat,
cues.zh: 对吧？一磅都没减。她们本应减掉，你知道，210磅脂肪，

cues.en: and they lost nothing.
cues.zh: 结果什么都没减。

cues.en: Right? Nothing. Right? It's not even... This is one one kilogram. So you're probably talking about, like, a quarter of a pound, you know, the weight of a good bowel movement or something like that. Right? Yeah.
cues.zh: 对吧？什么都没减。对吧？甚至都不是……这是一公斤。所以你说的大概是四分之一磅，你知道，一次顺畅排便的重量之类的。对吧？是的。

cues.en: It doesn't work.
cues.zh: 这没用。

cues.en: So we've known it for so long, and yet we keep telling people over and over and over, reduce your calories, reduce your calories, exercise more. We know it doesn't work.
cues.zh: 我们早就知道这一点，却还一遍又一遍地告诉人们：少吃点热量，少吃点热量，多运动。我们知道这没用。

cues.en: I could have told you that. And this again is the cruel hoax. Right? This is the cruel hoax because we we we put the blame on people when the blame should be on ourselves, the advice that we give, which is so poor.
cues.zh: 我早就跟你们说过。这又是一个残忍的骗局。对吧？这是个残忍的骗局，因为我们把责任推到人们身上，而责任其实应该在我们自己身上——在我们给出的那些糟糕透顶的建议上。

cues.en: So you eat less calories, you lose weight. Right? Your body senses that you lose weight. So you decrease your metabolism and increase your hunger. Right?
cues.zh: 所以你少吃热量，你就减重了。对吧？你的身体感知到你瘦了，于是降低代谢、增加饥饿感。对吧？

cues.en: Then you regain that weight.
cues.zh: 然后你又把体重涨回来了。

cues.en: But since you have a lot of willpower, you double down. Right? You're gonna eat even less calories. Right? And we've all done this. So you lose a bit more weight, but the problem is your body adjusts again, it reduces its metabolism
cues.zh: 但因为你有很强的意志力，你就加倍努力。对吧？你要吃更少的热量。对吧？我们都这么干过。于是你又减了一点，但问题是身体再次调整，降低代谢

cues.en: and increases your hunger,
cues.zh: 并增加你的饥饿感，

cues.en: and you start to regain the weight.
cues.zh: 然后你开始把体重涨回来。

cues.en: It keeps going on and on and on until you can't take it anymore because you feel lousy
cues.zh: 这样反复循环，直到你再也受不了，因为你感觉糟透了

cues.en: and the weight's still coming back.
cues.zh: 而体重还是照样回来。

cues.en: That's the cruel hoax,
cues.zh: 这就是那个残忍的骗局，

cues.en: right? And then,
cues.zh: 对吧？然后，

cues.en: to top it off,
cues.zh: 更糟的是，

cues.en: everybody thinks,
cues.zh: 所有人都觉得，

cues.en: Oh, yeah,
cues.zh: 哦，是啊，

cues.en: that guy,
cues.zh: 那家伙，

cues.en: he couldn't stick to his diet.
cues.zh: 他就是坚持不了自己的饮食计划。

cues.en: You know, the most unfair, like, the most cruel thing we do to people. And the ultimate proof is not in some kind of big study. The ultimate proof is in all of us. Right? I can show you all this, but, like, honestly, who hasn't done these sort of diets? Right? My guess is, like, ninety percent of the entire population of North America has been on some kind of diet like this at some point in their lives,
cues.zh: 你知道吗，这是我们能对别人做的最不公平、最残忍的事。最终的证据不在什么大型研究里。最终的证据就在我们每个人身上。对吧？我可以给你们看各种数据，但说实话，谁没试过这种饮食法？我猜，北美大概百分之九十的人，一生中某个时候都试过这类饮食法，

cues.en: and it didn't work.
cues.zh: 而它根本没用。

cues.en: Right? That's just the truth.
cues.zh: 对吧？这就是事实。

cues.en: Right? And this is the problem. Right? The problem is that you need to know which way you're going,
cues.zh: 对吧？问题就在这里。问题在于你得知道自己在往哪个方向走，

cues.en: and the problem is insulin because that's what tells the body which way to go. Right? Insulin
cues.zh: 而问题就出在胰岛素上，因为是它告诉身体该往哪走。对吧？胰岛素

cues.en: tells the body to store fat. That's what its normal job is. Right? When you eat, insulin goes up and you start to store fat. Right? You're not breaking any laws of thermodynamics.
cues.zh: 告诉身体去储存脂肪。这就是它的正常工作。对吧？你一吃东西，胰岛素就升高，你就开始储存脂肪。对吧？你并没有违反任何热力学定律。

cues.en: So what we see
cues.zh: 所以我们看到

cues.en: is that if you look at it from a hormonal obesity
cues.zh: 是，如果你从激素性肥胖

cues.en: point of view, right, if you're trying to really understand the etiology of obesity,
cues.zh: 的角度来看，对吧，如果你真的想搞懂肥胖的病因，

cues.en: what you see is that it's still too many calories in the end. Right?
cues.zh: 你会发现，说到底还是摄入卡路里太多。对吧？

cues.en: That's the proximate cause. That's not the ultimate cause. The ultimate cause is the insulin.
cues.zh: 那是直接原因，不是根本原因。根本原因是胰岛素。

cues.en: And if that is the ultimate cause, forget about this eat less, move more. That's not gonna be successful any more than drink less alcohol is more successful. The ultimate treatment is to lower insulin.
cues.zh: 而如果那才是根本原因，那就别管什么少吃多动了。那不会成功，就像少喝酒并不会更成功一样。根本的治疗方法是降低胰岛素。

cues.en: Now that you understand,
cues.zh: 现在你明白了，

cues.en: now you can design rational treatments.
cues.zh: 现在你就可以设计合理的治疗方案了。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: what's the evidence that insulin actually makes you fat? Well, there's all kinds of association studies, but the problem with association studies is that they don't tell you anything. Right? What you need are causation studies, and to do that, you have to give people stuff like insulin.
cues.zh: 有什么证据表明胰岛素真的会让你变胖？嗯，有各种各样的关联研究，但关联研究的问题在于它们什么都说明不了。对吧？你需要的是因果研究，而要做这个，你得给人用胰岛素之类的东西。

cues.en: So this is the DCCT
cues.zh: 所以这就是DCCT

cues.en: trial. Right? So this is type one diabetics.
cues.zh: 试验。对吧？这是一型糖尿病患者。

cues.en: And what they did is they had a group which had a lot of insulin and low blood sugars
cues.zh: 他们做的是，把一组人给大量胰岛素、血糖控制得低

cues.en: and another group which had not that much insulin and higher blood sugars. Now the group that had tight blood sugar controls did have less complications,
cues.zh: 另一组胰岛素不多、血糖较高。血糖严格控制的那组确实并发症更少，

cues.en: but that's not my question. Right? My question is,
cues.zh: 但这不是我的问题。对吧？我的问题是，

cues.en: does that insulin make you fat?
cues.zh: 这些胰岛素会让你发胖吗？

cues.en: And it does. So at the end of ten years, nine years, you can see that the people who got lots of insulin,
cues.zh: 确实会。所以在十年、九年结束时，你能看到那些用了大量胰岛素的人，

cues.en: like,
cues.zh: 大概，

cues.en: almost thirty percent of them had major weight problems.
cues.zh: 将近百分之三十的人有严重的体重问题。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: So I'm not saying that they shouldn't get it. I'm just saying that here's a actual causation study.
cues.zh: 所以我不是说他们不该用。我只是说，这是一个真实的因果研究。

cues.en: We gave the insulin.
cues.zh: 我们给了胰岛素。

cues.en: They got fat.
cues.zh: 他们变胖了。

cues.en: You can look at the correlation
cues.zh: 你可以看相关性

cues.en: between the total insulin dose
cues.zh: 在胰岛素总剂量

cues.en: and how much weight they gained.
cues.zh: 和他们增重多少之间。

cues.en: And it turns out it's actually pretty tight.
cues.zh: 结果发现相关性其实相当紧密。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: As you give more and more insulin, right, this is more and more insulin, you gain more and more weight. And again, as doctors,
cues.zh: 随着你给的胰岛素越来越多，对吧，这是越来越多的胰岛素，你体重增加得越来越多。再说一次，作为医生，

cues.en: this, you already know because we've all prescribed insulin and we all know it causes weight gain. Right?
cues.zh: 这个你早就知道了，因为我们都开过胰岛素，我们都知道它会导致体重增加。对吧？

cues.en: In type two diabetes, you see exactly the same thing. So this was the UKPDS.
cues.zh: 在2型糖尿病中，你看到完全一样的情况。这就是UKPDS。

cues.en: So, again, another trial where they gave people lots of drugs to control the blood sugars.
cues.zh: 所以，又是一个试验，他们给人们大量药物来控制血糖。

cues.en: And another drug, another arm,
cues.zh: 另一个药，另一个分组，

cues.en: which didn't get as much drug and had worse blood sugars. Again, that's not my question. My question is, does all this insulin make you fat?
cues.zh: 用的药没那么多，血糖更差。再说一次，这不是我的问题。我的问题是，这些胰岛素会让你发胖吗？

cues.en: And once again, you see that it is. So the intensively treated group,
cues.zh: 再一次，你就能看到确实如此。所以强化治疗组，

cues.en: which got a lot more insulin and a lot more drugs that stimulate insulin, gain more weight. So again, once again,
cues.zh: 他们用了更多胰岛素和更多刺激胰岛素的药物，体重增加得更多。所以再一次，

cues.en: moving us out of the correlation side, these are direct
cues.zh: 让我们脱离相关性层面，这些是直接的

cues.en: causal inferences.
cues.zh: 因果推断。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: There's a fascinating study
cues.zh: 有一项很有意思的研究

cues.en: done
cues.zh: 是

cues.en: in 1993 where they took these type two diabetics
cues.zh: 1993年做的，他们招募了这些2型糖尿病患者

cues.en: and they started off with no insulin. Right? And they said, well, what I'm going to do is I'm going to just amp up the insulin.
cues.zh: 一开始他们完全不用胰岛素。对吧？然后他们说，我要做的就是加大胰岛素剂量。

cues.en: Okay? Give them a lot of insulin. Their sugars are going be beautiful.
cues.zh: 好吗？给他们大量胰岛素。他们的血糖会变得很漂亮。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: And what they did was that they went from zero
cues.zh: 他们所做的就是从零

cues.en: to... At the beginning, they're not taking any insulin. By six months, they're taking a hundred units a day. Right? Their sugars are really, really well controlled.
cues.zh: 到……开始时，他们不用任何胰岛素。到六个月时，他们每天用一百单位。对吧？他们的血糖控制得非常好。

cues.en: But what happens to their weight? Again, you can see there's a steady rise. Right? Ninety three,
cues.zh: 但他们的体重发生了什么？同样，你能看到稳步上升。对吧？九十三、

cues.en: ninety seven, a 100, a hundred and two. So we're not talking again about correlations.
cues.zh: 九十七、一百、一百零二。所以我们再次说的不是相关性。

cues.en: We gave insulin,
cues.zh: 我们给了胰岛素，

cues.en: people gained weight. And what's actually interesting about this trial in particular was that they actually looked at how many calories they were eating, and the number of calories that they ate was reduced
cues.zh: 人们体重增加了。这项试验特别有意思的一点是，他们实际上还观察了受试者吃了多少卡路里，而他们摄入的卡路里数量减少了

cues.en: by about
cues.zh: 大约

cues.en: 300 calories per day, two fifty, 300.
So even as they lost,
cues.zh: 所以即使他们减少，

cues.en: even as they took less and less calories,
cues.zh: 即使他们摄入越来越少卡路里，

cues.en: right,
cues.zh: 对吧，

cues.en: they should have been losing weight according to the calorie theory,
cues.zh: 按照卡路里理论他们本应该减重，

cues.en: they gained,
cues.zh: 他们却增重了，

cues.en: like, 20 pounds.
cues.zh: 大概20磅。

cues.en: So you're eating less calories
cues.zh: 所以你摄入的卡路里更少

cues.en: and gaining 20 pounds. What's Well, you're giving insulin. Insulin's telling your body, store fat, store fat. That's its job. Right? So what's gonna happen is your body's gonna ramp down your metabolism until you store that fat.
cues.zh: 体重却增加了20磅。怎么回事呢？是你在给胰岛素。胰岛素在告诉你的身体，储存脂肪，储存脂肪。这就是它的职责。对吧？所以接下来会发生的是，你的身体会降低新陈代谢，直到你把那些脂肪储存起来。

cues.en: Right? Because that's what its job is.
cues.zh: 对吧？因为这就是它的职责。

cues.en: So you see the same thing with metformin. Metformin is a very interesting drug because it doesn't... It blocks gluconeogenesis
cues.zh: 所以你在二甲双胍上也看到同样的情况。二甲双胍是一种非常有趣的药物，因为它不……它阻断糖异生

cues.en: and doesn't raise insulin to the same extent. And what you find with that drug is that you don't get the same weight gain. So you see the conventional, so people who are just on diet control and the metformin group, they don't differ. But the ones who get sulfonylureas,
cues.zh: 而且不会把胰岛素升高到同样的程度。而用这种药物你会发现，体重不会同样增加。所以你看常规的，所以那些只靠饮食控制的人和二甲双胍组，他们没有差异。但那些使用磺脲类药物的，

cues.en: so drugs that stimulate insulin
cues.zh: 也就是刺激胰岛素的药物

cues.en: make you gain weight. So it's not just injecting insulin.
cues.zh: 会让你体重增加。所以不只是注射胰岛素。

cues.en: It's drugs that stimulate insulin do the same thing. And, again, as doctors, this is not a surprise.
cues.zh: 刺激胰岛素的药物也会做同样的事。而且，再说一次，作为医生，这并不意外。

cues.en: All these drugs, which are called sulfonylureas,
cues.zh: 所有这些药物，被称为磺脲类，

cues.en: stimulate insulin. So it's not simply because you're injecting it, it's exogenous.
cues.zh: 刺激胰岛素。所以这不仅仅是因为你在注射它，它是外源性的。

cues.en: It's that when you when you stimulate your own pancreas to release it, you gain weight.
cues.zh: 而是当你刺激你自己的胰腺释放它时，你就会体重增加。

cues.en: And the thing is that the the other... The flip side
cues.zh: 而问题是，另一个……反面

cues.en: is that if insulin is what's making you gain weight,
cues.zh: 是如果胰岛素是让你体重增加的原因，

cues.en: then if your insulin goes down, you would predict that you would lose weight,
cues.zh: 那么如果你的胰岛素下降，你会预测你会体重减轻，

cues.en: and that's exactly what happens. So this is a slide Eric showed.
cues.zh: 而这正是会发生的情况。所以这是Eric展示的一张幻灯片。

cues.en: So as your insulin goes down and down and down, what happens?
cues.zh: 当你的胰岛素一路下降，会发生什么？

cues.en: You can't gain weight. Right? The classic description of type one diabetes
cues.zh: 你没法增重。对吧？一型糖尿病的经典描述

cues.en: is a melting down of flesh and limbs into urine.
cues.zh: 就是血肉和四肢消融进尿液里。

cues.en: Right? It's a wonderful description.
cues.zh: 对吧？这描述真妙。

cues.en: But...
cues.zh: 但是……

cues.en: Because you just lose everything. No matter what you eat, you can give them anything. You can give them... No matter what you give them to eat, they have no insulin.
cues.zh: 因为你把一切都流失掉了。无论你吃什么，你可以给他们任何东西。你可以给他们……无论你给他们吃什么，他们都没有胰岛素。

cues.en: So they have no signal to store fat. They lose all their body fat, then they die. And that's unfortunately what happened until insulin came along.
cues.zh: 所以他们没有储存脂肪的信号。他们失去所有体脂，然后死去。不幸的是，在胰岛素出现之前，情况就是这样。

cues.en: And there's a a disease called diabulimia,
cues.zh: 还有一种病叫糖尿病贪食症（diabulimia），

cues.en: which is a
cues.zh: 这是一种

cues.en: eating disorder where type one diabetics will deliberately underdose
cues.zh: 进食障碍，一型糖尿病患者会故意少打

cues.en: their insulin. Right? So
cues.zh: 胰岛素。对吧？所以

cues.en: they... Their sugars go up and, you know, they could die of ketoacidosis.
cues.zh: 他们……血糖升高，你知道，他们可能死于酮症酸中毒。

cues.en: There's all kinds of problems. Right? So why do people do it? Because they lose weight.
cues.zh: 各种问题都有。对吧？那人们为什么这么做？因为他们能减重。

cues.en: They know it. We know it. When you cut their insulin, their weight goes down.
cues.zh: 他们知道，我们也知道。当你削减他们的胰岛素，他们的体重就下降。

cues.en: And recently, there's another drug which has done... Shown the same thing. So these are the SGLT two. So until recently, there were no other drugs really to lower insulin.
cues.zh: 而最近，还有另一种药物也做到了……显示了同样的效果。就是这些SGLT2抑制剂。所以直到最近，其实没有其他药物能降低胰岛素。

cues.en: But this drug,
cues.zh: 但这种药，

cues.en: which is a new drug that's approved for type two diabetes,
cues.zh: 这是一种获批用于二型糖尿病的新药，

cues.en: actually shows that you can lower insulin levels. Right? You make you pee out the sugar and your insulin levels go down. So these two groups, the DAPA group,
cues.zh: 实际上表明你可以降低胰岛素水平。对吧？你让糖从尿里排出，胰岛素水平就下降。所以这两组人，DAPA组，

cues.en: are the two groups that
cues.zh: 是这两组

cues.en: have this drug, and you can see that their insulin goes down. Right? And what happens?
cues.zh: 使用这种药的人，你可以看到他们的胰岛素下降了。对吧？然后发生了什么？

cues.en: Well, their weight goes down.
cues.zh: 他们的体重会下降。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: What's fascinating to me... So these are the three DAPA groups. So all of them showed weight loss.
cues.zh: 让我着迷的是……这是三个DAPA组。所有这些组都显示出体重减轻。

cues.en: And what's fascinating to me really when I look at something like this is that
cues.zh: 而当我看到这样的结果时，真正让我着迷的是

cues.en: you can follow these people out longer
cues.zh: 你可以追踪这些人更长时间

cues.en: to a year, two years, even four years now,
cues.zh: 到一年、两年，甚至现在的四年，

cues.en: and that weight stays off.
cues.zh: 体重一直保持下降。

cues.en: Right? And this is fascinating because if you look at virtually every single diet study available,
cues.zh: 对吧？这很令人着迷，因为如果你看几乎所有可获得的饮食研究，

cues.en: people's weight goes back up at around six months. It goes down. We all know this. Right? It goes back up.
cues.zh: 人们的体重在大约六个月时会回升。它先下降。我们都知道这一点。对吧？它又回升了。
